evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, contexts, values and planned figures are original. The set adapts only the mapped demands of intensity calculation and amplitude comparison.

questions.prompt: State what is meant by amplitude and state the relationship between the intensity and amplitude of a progressive wave.
A wave transfers 18 W uniformly through an area of 3.0 m² normal to its direction of energy transfer. What is its intensity?
The amplitude of a progressive wave becomes three times its original value. By what factor does its intensity change?

options.A: It becomes one third as large.
options.B: It becomes three times as large.
options.C: It becomes six times as large.
options.D: It becomes nine times as large.

questions.prompt: The intensity of a progressive wave falls to 0.49 of its original value. What is the new amplitude as a fraction of the original amplitude?
A progressive wave has amplitude 2.4 mm and intensity 32 W m⁻². Its amplitude is changed to 3.6 mm while the other relevant conditions are unchanged.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the ratio of the new amplitude to the original amplitude.

questions.prompt: Measurements for one progressive wave are plotted on axes of intensity I against amplitude A.

figure.purpose: Assess graph construction and interpretation of a square relationship.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white axes with horizontal amplitude A in mm from 0 to 4.0 and vertical intensity I in W m minus two from 0 to 40. Plot no points. Supply the data only in the prompt table: A/mm 0,1.0,2.0,3.0,4.0 and I/(W m^-2) 0,2.5,10,22.5,40.
figure.alt_text: Blank axes for plotting intensity against amplitude from the supplied data.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Plot the data and draw a smooth best-fit curve.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Describe the shape of the graph.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain how the plotted data support the relationship between intensity and amplitude.

questions.prompt: At detector X, a progressive wave has intensity 80 W m⁻² and amplitude 6.0 mm. At detector Y, the wave transfers 10 W uniformly through a sensing area of 0.50 m² normal to the energy transfer.

figure.purpose: Assess a two-stage power-area-to-amplitude comparison without exposing the method.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white line layout of detector X labelled I_X=80 W m^-2 and A_X=6.0 mm, and detector Y labelled P_Y=10 W and sensing area 0.50 m squared normal to energy flow. Use distinct symbols I, A for amplitude, P and area label S to avoid ambiguity. No formulas or results.
figure.alt_text: Detector X has known intensity and amplitude; detector Y has known power and normal sensing area.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the intensity at detector Y.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the ratio of the amplitude at Y to the amplitude at X.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Calculate the amplitude at detector Y and explain why it is smaller than at X.
